title: Pentaflex — interview notes, W. Deneckere (BBP contacts)
text:
PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL — OUTSIDE COUNSEL WORK PRODUCT

INTERVIEW NOTES

Matter: PENTAFLEX CONVEYOR BELTS NV — internal investigation (trade-association contacts)
Firm ref.: DH/2026/3862-PFX
Date: Wednesday 9 September 2026, 09:40–12:15
Place: offices of Pentaflex Conveyor Belts NV, Zwartebeekstraat 41, 2800 Mechelen (meeting room 2)
Present: Ms. Inès Rasquin (Partner, Duvivier Hasselbrink Advocaten); Mr. Tobias Eyckmans (Associate, same firm — note-taker); Ms. Saskia Verlinden (General Counsel, Pentaflex Conveyor Belts NV)
Interviewee: Mr. Wouter Deneckere, Sales Director Benelux, Pentaflex Conveyor Belts NV ("the Company"), employed since 2017

Preliminary

1. Ms. Rasquin gave the Upjohn warning: the Firm represents the Company, not the interviewee; the privilege belongs to the Company, which may waive it and disclose the content to third parties, incl. the Belgian Competition Authority or the European Commission. Deneckere confirmed he understood; no separate counsel requested. Litigation hold of 24 August 2026 acknowledged.

Background

2. Deneckere has attended meetings of Benelux Belting Producers VZW ("BBP"), the trade association, since 2019 as the Company's delegate to the sales & markets committee.
3. Regular attendees identified: for Griesbacher Fördergurte GmbH ("Griesbacher"), Mr. Klaus Hettinger (Vertriebsleiter Benelux); for Rondelaar Transportbanden BV ("Rondelaar"), Mr. Maarten Schouwenaar. Deneckere described Hettinger as "the one who does the talking".

Meetings

4. 12 March 2026, Hotel De Blauwe Reiger, Breda — BBP sales & markets committee. After the formal agenda (raw-material index, CBAM) Hettinger raised "the rubber surcharge" and said Griesbacher would apply 6% from 1 May. Schouwenaar said Rondelaar "would probably follow". Deneckere "said nothing"; the Company announced a 5.5% surcharge on 15 April 2026. Shown DOC-7315 (his email of 13 March 2026 to Pentaflex's pricing committee, subject "Breda — feedback"): accepted that "G. goes 6% in May, R. follows" refers to Griesbacher and Rondelaar.
5. 21 May 2026, Kastanjehof conference centre, Leuven — BBP general assembly. No commercial discussion in plenary. Over dinner Hettinger showed him on his phone a spreadsheet headed "volumes per key account"; Deneckere stated that he did not look closely and cannot recall the customers. Did not photograph it.
6. 18 June 2026, Hotel Löwenkranz, Cologne — bilateral; no BBP meeting scheduled. In Cologne for a customer visit; Hettinger suggested a coffee. The open quarry-conveyor tender (the Company's bid) was discussed, not "in numbers" per Deneckere. Shown DOC-7402 (calendar entry "KH — Löwenkranz 17:30" and mileage claim of 19 June 2026): confirmed both.
7. 3 September 2026, no physical meeting. Hettinger called him from +49 171 5539 2846 (saved as "KH mobil") asking whether the Company "was going to be reasonable on the Q4 list price". Deneckere stated that he ended the call within a minute; telephony export: 4 min 12 s. Confronted: "small talk about the holidays first".

Documents

8. DOC-7519 is the export of a WhatsApp group named "Belting Amigos BNL", created by Schouwenaar on 27 February 2026; members: Deneckere, Hettinger, Schouwenaar and one further Dutch mobile number not yet attributed. 214 messages. Deneckere: "mostly football"; acknowledged Hettinger's message of 20 April 2026, 22:14 — "all aligned on May then?" — answered with a thumbs-up. Left the group on 26 August 2026, two days after the litigation hold, and deleted the application; export recovered from the Company's MDM backup.
9. Hettinger also emailed him from k.hettinger@griesbacher-foerder.example.de on 22 April 2026 ("see attached, per our talk"), attachment "PL_Q3_draft.xlsx"; Deneckere stated that he did not open it. Preserved; to be numbered in the DOC-7519 series.

Awareness

10. Asked whether he knew that exchanging future prices and surcharges with competitors may infringe Article 101 TFEU and Article IV.1 of the Code of Economic Law: completed the Company's e-learning in 2023, knew "the rules on price fixing", thought "surcharge information is public anyway once announced". Ms. Rasquin referred to the Commission's Guidelines on horizontal cooperation agreements (chapter 6): exchange of intended future prices is restrictive by object. Nobody at the Company instructed him; he reported none of the contacts to Ms. Verlinden or his line manager.
11. The BBP secretary-general reads a "competition law reminder" at the start of each meeting and leaves before dinner.

Assessment (Counsel only)

12. Credibility: cooperative but minimising; two corrections when confronted with documents (items 4 and 7). Risk of further undisclosed contacts (fourth group member; June bilateral).
13. Exposure: possible concerted practice on surcharges and list prices in the Benelux; the 15 April 2026 announcement post-dates the Breda exchange. Leniency timing under the Belgian Competition Authority's 2020 leniency guidelines and, given effect on trade between Member States, the Commission's Leniency Notice; factor in Article 12 of Regulation (EC) No 1/2003 (exchange within the European Competition Network). Real risk that Griesbacher approaches the Belgian Competition Authority first.

Follow-up

14. Eyckmans: attribute the fourth group member via the MDM export; forensic image of Deneckere's Company phone by 14 September 2026.
15. Ms. Verlinden: extend the litigation hold to the four addressees of DOC-7315; suspend Deneckere's attendance at BBP meetings pending review; no contact with Hettinger or Schouwenaar.
16. Ms. Rasquin: interview the pricing committee chair (week of 14 September); leniency-timing memo for the board by 18 September 2026; consider withdrawing from the BBP sales & markets committee.
17. Deneckere to be re-interviewed after the forensic review. Confidentiality instruction repeated. Closed 12:15.

Notes taken by T. Eyckmans; reviewed by I. Rasquin on 10 September 2026. Not verbatim; not read back to the interviewee.
